why: No input parameters; returns a static server-info string built entirely from local config.
Only a boolean 'force' flag; builds an auth URL from static config constants, no caller data reaches any sink.

sink: unencoded ID concatenated into a Microsoft Graph API URL path passed whole to https.request(), which applies dot-segment (../) normalization at the wire level
why: eventId is a free-form caller-controlled string (no format/encoding). utils/graph-api.js builds the final URL by splitting the already-interpolated endpoint on '/' and encoding each resulting segment, but encodeURIComponent never touches '.' characters, so a value like 'X/../../messages/YYY' still splits into real path segments including literal '..' tokens; verified in utils/graph-api.js:36-38 that split happens after $-interpolation, and confirmed with a local Node http reproduction (v22.23.2) that https.request(url,...) normalizes those dot-segments before the request line is sent, letting a crafted eventId redirect this calendar-only tool's POST into a different same-token Graph endpoint (e.g. /v1.0/messages/YYY/cancel).
No arguments; only reads the local token cache and returns a fixed status string.
subject/start/end/attendees/body are placed only into a JSON POST body sent to the caller's own /me/events endpoint; none of them are used to build a URL path or command.

sink: unencoded ID concatenated into a Microsoft Graph API URL path passed whole to https.request(), which normalizes ../ dot-segments at the wire level
why: Same mechanism as cancel-event/delete-event: eventId is caller-controlled free text, merged into the endpoint template before utils/graph-api.js splits on '/' and per-segment-encodes, so literal '..' segments inside eventId survive encoding and are later resolved away by URL normalization before the request is sent, letting a crafted eventId redirect the POST to a different Graph resource under the caller's own token.

email/delete.js wraps emailId in encodeURIComponent() directly (before template interpolation), which encodes any literal '/' in the ID so it cannot become an extra path segment -- verified this defeats the dot-segment injection that affects the unencoded-ID tools in this repo.

sink: unencoded ID used verbatim as the full Graph API URL path for a DELETE request
why: eventId is caller-controlled and unencoded before template interpolation. Reproduced with a local http server (matching this exact https.request(url,{method}) pattern, Node v22.23.2) that eventId='../../messages/YYY' turns the constructed path into the literal wire path '/v1.0/messages/YYY'; applied here, a crafted eventId lets a DELETE intended only for a calendar event instead delete an arbitrary same-token Graph resource, which is a genuine authorization-scope violation, not mere robustness.
to/cc/bcc/subject/body go only into a JSON POST body sent to the fixed me/messages endpoint; no path/command construction from caller input.

ruleName is only compared client-side (rule.displayName === ruleName) to select a rule object already fetched from the API; the ID actually placed in the PATCH endpoint (rule.id) comes from that API response, not from caller input.

sink: unencoded ID interpolated into a Power Automate Flow API path; power-automate/flow-api.js builds the final URL with new URL(fullUrl), which normalizes ../ dot-segments before extracting options.path for https.request
why: environmentId is caller-controlled free text with zero encoding anywhere in the chain (flow-api.js does not even per-segment-encode, unlike the Graph client). Reproduced with Node's URL constructor (node -e, v22.23.2) that environmentId='../../../connections/evilConn' turns the intended path into '/connections/evilConn/flows' on the same host, using the caller's Flow bearer token -- redirecting a fleet/environment-scoped listing into an arbitrary sibling Flow API resource.
contract: List flows in a Power Platform environment

why: Calls a fixed '/environments' path with no caller-supplied ID; no injectable argument reaches the URL.

sink: two unencoded IDs interpolated into a Flow API path that is later normalized by new URL() before the request is sent
why: Same unguarded interpolation as flow-list; either environmentId or flowId containing '../' segments is normalized away by new URL(fullUrl) in power-automate/flow-api.js (verified: node v22.23.2 new URL() reproduction), letting the caller redirect this GET to a different Flow API resource under the same access token.
contract: Get run history for a flow

sink: two unencoded IDs interpolated into a Flow API path, normalized by new URL() before the POST is sent (with attacker-controlled 'inputs' as the JSON body)
why: Same mechanism as flow-list/flow-list-runs. Because this handler issues a POST with a caller-controlled JSON body ('inputs'), a crafted environmentId/flowId could redirect the POST to a different Flow API endpoint that accepts that verb, combining path redirection with attacker-supplied payload delivery under the caller's own Flow token.

sink: two unencoded IDs interpolated into a Flow API path, normalized by new URL() before the POST (start/stop) is sent
why: Same unguarded interpolation as the other Power Automate tools; a crafted environmentId/flowId is normalized by new URL(fullUrl) in flow-api.js, letting a call meant only to start/stop one specific flow redirect its POST to a different Flow API path with the caller's own token.

A crafted ID containing '../' segments is normalized by the underlying https.request(url) call, letting the caller redirect the POST to a different Graph resource than the target message, still mutating it via the caller's own token.

sink: unencoded item ID used as the Graph API URL path, later normalized by https.request's URL parsing before the request is sent
why: itemId is caller-controlled and unencoded. Empirically reproduced (node v22.23.2, http server matching the exact https.request(url) pattern used here) that itemId='../../messages/YYY' makes the wire-level request path resolve to a different resource than the intended drive item, so a crafted itemId can make this OneDrive-only tool fetch (and return a '@microsoft.graph.downloadUrl'-shaped view of) a different Graph resource such as a message, using the caller's own bearer token.
contract: Get a download URL for a file in OneDrive. Either 'itemId' or 'path' must be provided.

why: 'path' is a hierarchical OneDrive path by design; normalization only ever redirects within the caller's own root:/...:/children addressing scheme and lands on malformed/non-existent endpoints rather than a clean alternate resource (the fixed 'root:' / ':children' template segments make a clean redirect impractical, unlike the opaque-ID tools).
query is passed through encodeURIComponent() before being embedded in the search(q='...') endpoint, preventing it from introducing extra path structure.

sink: unencoded item ID (when supplied directly, resolvedItemId===itemId) used in a Graph API URL path for a POST that creates a sharing link
why: When the caller supplies itemId directly (the tool's own schema offers itemId as an alternative to path), it is used completely unencoded. Same reproducible mechanism as onedrive-download/onedrive-delete: a crafted itemId with '../' segments is normalized away by the https.request(url) call, letting the caller redirect the POST that creates an (anonymous, by default) sharing link to a different Graph resource than intended -- a confidentiality-relevant redirection since the tool's whole purpose is exposing a link to whatever resource the ID resolves to.
contract: Create a sharing link for a file or folder in OneDrive

why: 'path' is a hierarchical destination path by design; content is sent as the PUT body, not used to build the URL.
